notes: AST/dataflow rule: inter-procedural (intra-module) const/taint propagation catches VARIABLE-MEDIATED injection the line-oriented regex rules provably miss (a dangerous value assembled in one statement, used in a later statement) PLUS cross-function helper returns and sink aliases. Sinks: eval/new Function (ast-eval-injection, high), child_process exec/execSync + spawn(shell:true) (ast-command-injection, critical), .query/.execute/.raw with a dynamic SQL-shaped non-parameterized arg (ast-sql-injection, high). fpMode any — ANY finding on a negative is an FP. The hard FP guards are: const-propagation (a variable bound only to constant strings is CONST-SAFE and never flagged, incl. the prototype's `const q=`SELECT 1`; db.query(q)` FP); the SQL-keyword gate (a dynamic .query arg only flags when real SQL text is recovered); and the params-array exemption. INTER-PROCEDURAL upgrade: arg-sensitive local-function return-taint resolution binds a helper's params to the call site's arg classifications and recovers BOTH dynamic + static SQL text (cycle-guarded, depth-limited ~6) — so `function build(x){return "SELECT "+x} db.query(build(req.id))` flags while `build(){return "SELECT 1"} db.query(build())` and `id(x){return x} db.query(id("SELECT 1"))` stay clean. SINK-ALIAS resolution: `const X = obj.query|execute|raw|exec|execSync` (simple non-reassigned const) makes a later `X(arg)` the same sink, while `const run=console.log; run(...)` is NOT a sink. Unknown/non-local calls stay structurally dynamic with NO recovered text (keyword gate still guards). Positives are SYNTHETIC (honest).
